Proposal from the candidate side:

**Appointment:** 12-month methods-desk appointment starting [date]. Schedule: **3 days/week through February; 4 days/week from March onward**. The March move to 4 days is a capacity commitment, not conditioned on the outside project. Suggested core days: Tue–Thu now; add Monday or Friday from March, flexible around publication deadlines. Title and review milestone are open: e.g., “Methods Desk Lead,” with a written review at the March transition and again at month six.

**Compensation:** **$125,000 as the 1.0 FTE base**. Pay follows actual FTE—0.60 through February, 0.80 from March—unless Finch intends $125,000 cash for part-time service, which is a different, premium ask. Benefits/bonus: pro rata, or a stipend if part-time thresholds apply; resolve in the term sheet.

**Editorial control:** Noor has **final say over methods-desk content and corrections**—whether to correct, wording, placement, and timing—except where law compels action, and even then the methods wording remains Noor’s. Finch may do legal/style review but cannot override substantive methods judgments.

**Outside project firewall:** Noor continues an existing outside editorial project independently. Its **data, source materials, unfinished articles, and outputs are not assigned, licensed, or made available to Finch**; Finch gets no access and no derivative rights. Noor will not use Finch time, systems, or staff for it, will recuse from Finch matters involving it or its funders/partners/competitors, and the parties will sign a short conflict schedule. New work created for Finch on Finch days belongs to Finch; pre-existing IP remains Noor’s and is licensed, not assigned, unless separately agreed.

**Tradeoffs:** The candidate can be flexible on title, exact review date, and core days. In return, the needed terms are the $125k FTE basis, final say on methods corrections, and the firewall above. If Finch wants an earlier move to 4 days, more days, or any rights in the outside project, those are separate concessions and should be priced explicitly.

Please respond on: start date/term, comp basis, final-say wording, firewall/conflict schedule, benefits, and preferred title/review dates.

Finch proposes a 12-month appointment as **Methods Desk Lead**, from December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027. We can meet the **$125,000 full-time-equivalent base** if Noor trains the deputy. We can also keep Noor’s three-day schedule through February and open the desk to submissions four days a week from its first week.

- **Coverage and pay.** The desk takes submissions Tuesday through Friday. Through February, Noor works Tuesday through Thursday at 0.60 FTE, a $75,000 annual pay rate. The deputy covers Friday. From March 1, Noor works all four days at 0.80 FTE, a $100,000 annual pay rate, regardless of the outside project’s schedule. Training and handoffs count toward Noor’s scheduled time.
- **Deputy review.** Before the first Friday, Noor and the deputy will document how to log submissions, flag urgent concerns, and hand cases back. The deputy can acknowledge submissions and request missing materials. Routine methods judgments go to Noor on Tuesday. Urgent accuracy concerns go directly to the editor-in-chief on Friday, with the concern and any action recorded for Noor’s review.
- **Corrections and publication.** Noor leads the methods assessment and recommends whether to correct, with proposed wording, placement, and timing. If the editor-in-chief disagrees, Noor and the editor confer within one working day. If disagreement persists, either can request a prompt assessment from an uninvolved methods editor. The editor-in-chief retains final authority over publication and corrections and records the decision and reasons alongside Noor’s recommendation. The editor-in-chief may post an interim reader notice immediately when delay risks misleading readers. Finch will not attribute a conclusion to Noor without Noor’s agreement.
- **Outside project.** We accept the proposed firewall for the project’s remaining nine months. Finch gets no access or rights to its materials or outputs. Before the start date, we’ll agree on a conflict schedule covering the project, its funders, partners, and identified competitors. Noor will flag new conflicts and route affected submissions directly to an unconflicted editor without reviewing them. Finch owns work Noor creates for Finch. Any use of Noor’s pre-existing materials requires a separately agreed license.
- **Benefits and reviews.** We propose prorated paid leave and prorated participation in any applicable bonus plan. If a part-time threshold prevents health coverage, we propose a stipend equal to Finch’s usual employer contribution scaled to Noor’s FTE. We’ll put eligibility and the dollar amount in the term sheet before signature. We propose written reviews on March 1 and June 1 covering desk coverage, deputy readiness, and how disputed corrections were handled. The March schedule change takes effect automatically.

Can Noor accept responsibility for training the deputy at the requested base, and the editor-in-chief’s final decision on disputed corrections under this process?

Response on the two open questions and the remaining terms:

**Accepted as proposed:**
- Title **Methods Desk Lead**; term **December 1, 2026 – November 30, 2027**.
- **$125,000 FTE base**: Tue–Thu at 0.60 FTE ($75,000) through February; Tue–Fri at 0.80 FTE ($100,000) from March 1, automatic, independent of the outside project. This matches the full-time-annualized figure Noor requires.
- Desk open to submissions four days a week from week one, deputy covering Friday.
- Outside-project firewall and pre-start conflict schedule as you drafted, including routing of conflicted submissions to an unconflicted editor.
- Prorated leave/bonus, health stipend if the part-time threshold blocks coverage, with eligibility and amount in the term sheet. Reviews March 1 and June 1.

**Training the deputy — yes, with two clarifications.** Training and handoffs happen inside Noor's scheduled hours (as you proposed). Add: the written handoff protocol is completed before the first Friday, and deputy readiness is assessed at the March 1 review. If the deputy is not ready by March 1, Friday coverage continues at Finch's arrangement and cost — it does not reduce Noor's hours or pay, and the March move to 0.80 FTE still takes effect automatically.

**Editor-in-chief final authority on disputed corrections — Noor cannot accept that.** Final say over methods corrections is a core term for the candidate. Here is the counter that preserves Finch's legitimate urgency interest:

- **Noor's decision is final on methods corrections** — whether to correct, and the wording, placement, and timing — except where law compels action.
- The **editor-in-chief may post an interim reader notice immediately** when delay risks misleading readers, but the notice will not attribute any conclusion to Noor without Noor's agreement, and the substantive correction — its wording, placement, and timing — returns to Noor for final decision within one working day.
- Your escalation step stays, but as **advisory, not binding**: an uninvolved methods editor may assess promptly, and Noor and the editor-in-chief confer within one working day. Whatever is decided, the decision and both positions are recorded and reviewed at the June 1 review.
- **Friday urgent concerns**: the deputy or editor-in-chief may acknowledge and post an interim notice, but the final methods call goes to Noor on an async basis within one working day — or to a methods editor Noor designates in writing before the first Friday, with that delegation recorded.

**Tradeoff, stated plainly:** the candidate gives Finch the interim-notice right, the recording/transparency mechanism, and the advisory review — everything needed to act fast on reader harm and to audit decisions later. What the candidate cannot give is a binding override of Noor's methods judgment by anyone at Finch. If Finch wants that override, it is a different package and would need to be priced as such.

Please confirm: (1) final-say wording as countered above, (2) the two training clarifications, (3) the term sheet items — benefits eligibility, stipend amount, start date, core days, and the conflict schedule draft.

Finch can offer a **$128,000 full-time-equivalent base**, including deputy training, if we settle the corrections clause below. That gives Noor annual pay rates of $76,800 at 0.60 FTE through February and $102,400 at 0.80 FTE from March 1.

**Disputed corrections.** Noor has final say over the substance and wording of Noor’s signed methods assessment. The editor-in-chief has final say over whether Finch publishes a correction, its wording, placement, and timing. If the editor-in-chief reaches a different conclusion, Finch will issue any resulting correction in its own name. Noor’s assessment will stand as written in the editorial record. Finch will seek Noor’s agreement before attributing a conclusion to Noor.

The editor-in-chief may post an interim reader notice immediately. Noor and the editor-in-chief will confer within one working day of a dispute, and either may seek an advisory assessment from an uninvolved methods editor. For urgent issues on Noor’s days off, Noor may designate a methods editor in writing before the first Friday to handle that consultation. Finch will record both positions, the decision, and its reasons for the June 1 review.

**Deputy training.** We accept both clarifications. Noor and the deputy will complete the written handoff protocol during Noor’s scheduled hours before Friday, December 4. Finch will assess readiness on March 1 and arrange and pay for any continuing Friday support. Noor’s move to Tuesday–Friday at 0.80 FTE takes effect automatically that day, with the agreed hours and pay regardless of deputy readiness.

**Term sheet.** The Methods Desk Lead appointment runs December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027. Noor works Tuesday–Thursday through February, with the deputy covering Friday intake, then Tuesday–Friday from March. Reviews are March 1 and June 1. Leave and any applicable bonus are prorated. Finch will specify health coverage eligibility at each FTE and, where the part-time threshold prevents coverage, the monthly stipend in dollars before signature. The stipend will equal the usual employer contribution multiplied by the applicable FTE. The dollar figures are still pending.

**Draft conflict schedule.** Noor will identify the outside project, its funders, partners, and relevant competitors before the start date and update the schedule as conflicts arise. Finch will designate an unconflicted editor to receive affected submissions directly. Noor will recuse from review and decisions on those matters and keep the project’s time, systems, staff, and materials separate from Finch’s. Finch has no access or rights to the project’s data, sources, drafts, or outputs. Those protections continue after the project ends.

Can Noor accept the $128,000 FTE package with final authority over Noor’s signed assessment and the editor-in-chief accountable for the correction Finch publishes?

Response from the candidate side:

**Accepted: $128,000 FTE base.** That exceeds the $125,000 full-time-annualized requirement — $76,800 at 0.60 FTE through February, $102,400 at 0.80 FTE from March 1, automatic, independent of the outside project and of deputy readiness. Deputy training accepted with both clarifications, including the written handoff protocol completed in Noor's scheduled hours before Friday, December 4, and Finch-funded Friday support if readiness lags.

**Corrections clause: acceptable, with one addition.** The candidate accepts the split as you've framed it — Noor has final say over the substance and wording of Noor's signed methods assessment, and that assessment stands unaltered in the editorial record; the editor-in-chief's publication decision is Finch's own, issued in Finch's name, with no attribution or paraphrase of Noor's conclusion without Noor's agreement. To make that workable in practice, add one sentence: **where Finch publishes a correction that differs from Noor's signed assessment, the published notice and the internal record must both preserve Noor's assessment verbatim, and the disagreement is expressly carried into the June 1 review.** Noor's methods judgment cannot be edited, overridden, or attributed away; Finch's accountability for what it publishes in its own name is the corresponding tradeoff, and the candidate accepts it. The interim-notice right, one-working-day conferral, advisory assessment, off-day designee, and recording of both positions all stand as drafted.

**Remaining items to close before signature — please put in the term sheet:**
1. **Health coverage eligibility at 0.60 and 0.80 FTE, and the monthly stipend dollar amount** where the part-time threshold blocks coverage (usual employer contribution × applicable FTE). These must be specified in dollars, not formulas.
2. **Conflict schedule**: Noor will identify the outside project, its funders, partners, and relevant competitors before December 1, 2026, with the firewall language as drafted — no Finch access or rights to the project's data, sources, drafts, or outputs, separation of time/systems/staff/materials, recusal and direct routing of affected submissions to the designated unconflicted editor, and protections surviving the project's end.
3. Confirmation of the full package: Methods Desk Lead, December 1, 2026 – November 30, 2027; Tue–Thu through February with deputy Friday intake; Tue–Fri from March 1; desk open to submissions four days a week from week one; prorated leave and bonus; written reviews March 1 and June 1 covering coverage, deputy readiness, and disputed-correction handling.

Send the term sheet with the stipend figures and the conflict schedule draft, and this is ready to close.

**Finch Review | Proposed appointment term sheet**

Two items remain open before signature. Finch proposes the publication language below for disputed corrections. Finch also owes Noor verified health eligibility and monthly stipend figures for both schedules.

| Term | Finch’s commitment |
|---|---|
| Appointment | Methods Desk Lead, December 1, 2026 through November 30, 2027. |
| Desk coverage | The desk takes submissions Tuesday through Friday from week one. Noor works Tuesday through Thursday through February, with the deputy covering Friday intake. From March 1, Noor works Tuesday through Friday. |
| Compensation | $128,000 full-time-equivalent base, including deputy training. The annual pay rate is $76,800 at 0.60 FTE through February and $102,400 at 0.80 FTE from March 1. The increase takes effect automatically regardless of deputy readiness or the outside project’s status. |
| Training and handoffs | Noor trains the deputy during scheduled hours. Together they will complete the written handoff protocol before Friday, December 4. The deputy logs submissions, acknowledges receipt, requests missing materials, and escalates urgent accuracy concerns to the editor-in-chief. Routine methods decisions go to Noor on Tuesday. Finch arranges and funds any additional Friday support needed after the March readiness review. |
| Benefits | Leave and any applicable bonus are prorated. Health eligibility at each FTE and Finch’s usual monthly employer contribution are still unverified. Finch will enter the coverage status and exact monthly stipend payable, if any, for each schedule before signature. Where the part-time threshold blocks coverage, Finch will pay the agreed FTE share of its usual contribution. |
| Written reviews | March 1 and June 1, covering desk coverage, deputy readiness, and handling of disputed corrections. |

**Disputed corrections.** Noor controls the substance and wording of Noor’s signed methods assessment. Finch will preserve it verbatim in the internal editorial record alongside both positions, the editor-in-chief’s decision, and the reasons. The editor-in-chief retains final authority over whether, when, where, and in what wording Finch publishes a correction. Finch issues the correction in its own name and must obtain Noor’s agreement before attributing or paraphrasing Noor’s conclusion.

Finch proposes this sentence for a correction that differs from the signed assessment: **The published notice will disclose that Finch’s decision differs from the signed methods assessment. Finch may also publish the assessment verbatim with Noor’s consent and the editor-in-chief’s approval.** Every such disagreement arising by June 1 will be addressed expressly at that review. This gives readers notice of the disagreement while preserving both parties’ authority over publication and attribution.

The editor-in-chief may post an immediate interim notice when delay risks misleading readers. The editor-in-chief and Noor will confer within one working day, and either may seek prompt advisory review by an uninvolved methods editor. Noor may designate a methods editor in writing before the first Friday to handle urgent consultations on Noor’s days off.

**Draft conflict schedule.** Before December 1, Noor will list the outside project, its funders, partners, and relevant competitors. Finch will name an unconflicted editor to receive affected submissions directly. Noor will update the schedule as conflicts arise and recuse from review and decisions on affected matters. Noor will keep the project’s time, systems, staff, and materials separate from Finch’s. Finch receives no access, license, or other rights to the project’s data, source materials, drafts, or outputs. Those protections survive the project’s end. Finch owns work Noor creates for Finch. Any use of Noor’s pre-existing materials requires a separate license.

Please confirm whether the public disclosure sentence resolves the corrections clause. Finch remains responsible for supplying the outstanding benefits figures before signature.

Confirmed, with one clarifying amendment to the disclosure sentence.

**The public disclosure sentence resolves the corrections clause** — Noor's signed assessment controls its own substance and wording and is preserved verbatim in the internal record; Finch's publication decision is Finch's own, issued in Finch's name; every disagreement is expressly carried into the June 1 review. The candidate accepts this split.

**One amendment:** the published disclosure shall state that Finch's decision differs from the signed methods assessment, but **will not identify Noor as the assessment's author, characterize the assessment, or attribute any conclusion to Noor without Noor's agreement**; verbatim publication of the assessment occurs only with Noor's consent and the editor-in-chief's approval. Same rule applies to any interim reader notice. With that sentence added, the corrections clause is closed.

**Everything else in the term sheet is accepted as written:** appointment December 1, 2026 – November 30, 2027; desk open Tuesday–Friday from week one; Tue–Thu through February with deputy Friday intake; Tue–Fri from March 1 at 0.80 FTE, automatic and independent of deputy readiness or the outside project; $128,000 FTE base ($76,800 / $102,400); training in scheduled hours with the written handoff protocol before December 4; prorated leave and bonus; March 1 and June 1 written reviews; and the conflict schedule as drafted, with protections surviving the project's end and pre-existing materials licensed only by separate agreement.

**Still open before signature, owed by Finch:** verified health-coverage eligibility at 0.60 and 0.80 FTE and the exact monthly stipend dollar amount for each schedule where the part-time threshold blocks coverage. The candidate will not sign on formulas; the figures must be in the term sheet.

Send the term sheet with those dollar figures and the amended disclosure sentence, and this closes.

Finch accepts the amendment. The term sheet’s disclosure clause now reads:

> When Finch publishes a correction that differs from the signed methods assessment, the notice will disclose that difference. Any further characterization of the assessment, identification of Noor as its author, or attribution or paraphrase of Noor’s conclusion requires Noor’s agreement. The same protections apply to interim reader notices. Verbatim publication of the assessment requires both Noor’s consent and the editor-in-chief’s approval.

The corrections clause is closed. **Health benefits are the sole outstanding item before signature.** Finch has yet to verify the plan’s eligibility threshold and its usual monthly employer contribution, so the coverage status and exact stipend for each schedule remain pending. Finch owes Noor a completed benefits entry for 0.60 FTE and another for 0.80 FTE, each stating eligibility and the monthly stipend in dollars. No further input is needed from Noor.
